text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000007 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation, with elevated shares even on 0–1 condition patients, but records are too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims data lean toward concern. The excess 99215 share holds in every complexity band, not only the sicker patients. A large part of the 99215 volume sits on patients with no or one chronic condition, and the sampled low-complexity claims show single symptom codes such as R10.9, R21 and N39.0 (for example C0001538, C0002102, C0002156). The panel does include genuinely complex patients (for example C0001935, C0002110), and all 4 documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM. That support is reassuring, but 4 charts out of roughly 200 99215 claims is too few to judge, and none of the documented charts are known to be low-complexity cases. The 2 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim are only weak evidence of possible note inflation. A reviewer should first request records for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, checking whether MDM and time genuinely support level 5 and whether the notes look templated or cloned."}
